title: Each plain letter keeps its own counter into a key word (homophone cycling) on known keyword tableaux: dictionary words and K1-K3 phrases, any-letter keys to length 5, row restarts, 3-4 fixed alphabets in turn
k4_result: 24,011,697 key-stream readings (666,993 alphabets x up to 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort/variant x key-letter alphabet), each against 264,690 key words and K1-K3 phrase windows (6.36e12 word-reading pairs, by an index). 8 pairs hold all 7 neighbour pairs, 0 hold the chains exactly, 0 texts hold the 24 clue letters. Any-letter keys of length 1-5: 0 of 6,669,918 key streams fit. Row restarts (168 tests, widths 2-48, carved rows included): 0 passes at 6 checks, 0 at 7+ (chance 0.22 and 0.01). Three fixed alphabets in turn: 186 pairs explain 16+ clue letters, 0 full sets of three. Nothing to read (best English -99; needs -5.1). Proofs: a common numeric step per occurrence, counters restarting at each word, keys of 1-2 letters and any 2 tableaux in turn are impossible for every tableau.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, every alphabet each (same 24.0M readings): neighbour-pair hits 2, 4, 31; chains held 0, 0, 0; any-letter rings 0, 0, 0; row tests 0, 0, 0; pairs explaining 16+ 24, 16, 306 with 0, 0, 0 full sets of three; texts holding the clues 0, 0, 0. Same picture as K4.
planted: 6/6 (COMPASS on a dictionary tableau, Vigenere; PALIMPSEST on a transposition-mixed dictionary tableau, Beaufort; ABSCISSA on KRYPTOS, variant, natural text with its own clue letters; a 4-letter non-word key; SHADOW with counters restarting at the carved rows; three different fixed alphabets in turn). Texts read back at 91-96 of 97 letters, English -4.02 to -4.74; no survivor read anything else.
scope_limits: Tableaux must be known: A-Z, KRYPTOS, 222k dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms, in 5 layouts; hidden alphabets are not covered (3 or 4 hidden tableaux picked by the counter always fit the clues, shown by exact search). Keys: dictionary/theme words of 3+ letters and 4-26 letter windows of K1-K3's plaintexts, or ANY letters up to length 5. Longer keys that are not in the list, and a separate key per letter, cannot be decided. All counters start at 0 at the first letter (every rotation of the word tried); counters that carry over from K1-K3 or start at different places per letter are not covered. Row restarts: only tests with 6+ checks, which needs a restart inside a clue block; row layouts whose breaks miss both clue blocks are not tested. Four fixed alphabets: only the bound on A-Z, KRYPTOS and 84 theme alphabets (at most 23 of 24 letters); dictionary scale not decided. The pre-filter FLAGs the K5 statement (same words in the same places would not encrypt alike unless the letter counts before them match); built anyway because the test is exact and cheap. Side finding: the cipher is not uniquely decipherable (letters can swap where their next key letters collide), which itself argues against it as a hand system.

negative.family: Per-letter counters into a key word (homophone cycling)
negative.hypothesis: K4 is C = Tab(P, W[n mod L]) with n the number of earlier occurrences of that plain letter: each plain letter steps through the key word W on its own.
negative.scope: 666,993 known alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword and two mixed forms) x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort/variant x key letter read in plain, cipher or A-Z alphabet = 24.0M readings; keys = 264,690 dictionary words and K1-K3 phrase windows, plus any-letter keys of length 1-5; counters from 0 with every rotation; variants: restart at rows of width 2-48 (168 tests with 6+ checks, carved rows included), three fixed alphabets in turn (exact join), four on 86 small alphabets (bound).
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 0 keys hold the clue chains and 0 texts hold the 24 clue letters (3 shuffled K4s on every alphabet: 0, 0, 0); 0 short rings, 0 row-restart passes, 0 sets of three alphabets (controls the same); planted 6/6 read back. Common step per occurrence, restart at each word, keys of 1-2 letters and 2 tableaux in turn are impossible by proof for every tableau.

follow_ups: The same per-letter counter with the counter kept on the CIPHER side (the key letter depends on how often this cipher letter has been written so far). Inside the clues the repeats are Q 26-27, R 24-29, S 33-34, T 68-69, P 66-73, V 25-67(gap), K 32-74(gap): 5 neighbour pairs, so the same word-index join works, and decryption is then unambiguous, which removes the objection found here.

Per-letter counters where the counter does not restart with K4 but carries over from K1-K3's plaintext (336+97+... letters): the counts at K4's start are then known numbers per letter, so the main test is the same with fixed, different rotations per letter; one extra loop over which sections count.
